grh_d02f849e5809273d91d8.title: Fool's Gold
paragraphs: Harry is recruited into a plan to hijack a valuable gold shipment in the Middle East and fly it to India for a huge black-market profit. He, Clancy and Singh pose as travelers and mechanics, divert the shipment onto a cart, load the heavy crates into their plane and escape with what Harry believes could bring nearly a million dollars. The operation begins to unravel when Professor Solomon and Filoura recognize what is happening and alert contacts ahead. Harry races the stolen cargo toward a buyer named Parenda, only to discover Parenda is already cooperating with police. Clancy and Singh are arrested and Harry's dream of a fortune collapses into a modest reward for supposedly helping recover the gold.

This [[show|the-lives-of-harry-lime|The Lives of Harry Lime]] broadcast aired on April 4, 1952. It is listed as episode 36 in the archive. The cast includes [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] and Anton Karas. Other credited names include Tig Roe as director and Harry Alan Towers as producer.

grh_d0f9a7e6c137ed020d72.title: The Senator Was Indiscreet
paragraphs: Vain but spectacularly inept Senator Melvin G. Ashton decides that his growing publicity proves the country wants him for president, while his press agent Luke Gibson struggles to contain the damage and marry sharp-tongued columnist Poppy McNaughton. As Ashton's accidental popularity grows, everyone around him worries about the private diary in which he has recorded years of political secrets and indiscretions. Poppy finally gets hold of the diary and sends it toward the newspapers just as Ashton convinces himself the White House is within reach. Realizing publication will destroy him, the senator abruptly abandons the presidential campaign and starts dreaming instead of being summoned to lead somewhere as remote as Outer Mongolia.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.

grh_d0f72e3f85b84fb65e85.title: Hired Wife
paragraphs: Businessman Stephen Dexter faces a legal attack that could seize everything he owns, and his lawyer finds one loophole: if Stephen marries and places the assets in his wife's name, the creditors cannot reach them. Stephen plans to marry glamorous Phyllis, while efficient secretary Kendall Browning organizes the rescue and becomes the practical woman he actually depends on. As the scheme unfolds, Stephen discovers Phyllis is interested in his fortune while Kendall truly loves him, turning the hired marriage arrangement into a genuine one.
